objective: Harden unattended Hermes worker execution in two ways: (1) prevent Windows QuickEdit/Select mode from pausing a visible worker and its watchdog, while preserving visible streaming; and (2) change recoverable worker-failure handling so the same task is retried automatically up to TWO times before it is finally marked blocked and the queue advances. Add regression/evidence for both behaviors.
allowed_scope: Inspect remote_queue/visible_worker.py, remote_queue/hermes_dispatch.py, remote_queue/poller.py, queue lifecycle helpers, and the Windows console launch path.

Implement the smallest safe Windows-specific hardening that prevents QuickEdit/Select mode from suspending worker progress while preserving the visible terminal requirement. Prefer disabling ENABLE_QUICK_EDIT_MODE for the worker console process only; do not hide the worker window and do not change the owner's global console preferences.

Implement bounded automatic retry for recoverable execution failures: initial attempt + at most TWO retries of the same task. Preserve landed commits/evidence between attempts; never redo successful work unnecessarily.

Do not retry owner-gated states, missing credentials, explicit safety/architecture/irreversible-action blockers, or other deterministic blockers that cannot change without owner/external action. Those should park immediately and allow independent work to continue.
Track retry count deterministically in queue/task runtime state or equivalent auditable metadata so retries cannot loop forever. After two failed retries, mark the task blocked and move on.
Keep existing hard task timeout and no-progress watchdog fail-closed behavior; a watchdog/CLI execution error is eligible for bounded retry unless evidence shows it is deterministic/non-recoverable.
Add isolated tests and record exact verification/evidence.
Do not mutate any currently running task contract; commit/push recoverably.
stop_conditions: Do not create infinite retry loops; maximum is two retries after the initial attempt.
Do not retry missing-key, owner-approval, architecture, safety, irreversible-action, or external-provider blockers unless the relevant state has actually changed.
Do not kill unrelated processes or modify global console settings destructively.
Do not expose secrets or weaken watchdog/timeouts.
If per-process Windows console mode cannot be changed safely, record the exact limitation and leave global settings unchanged.
notes: Triggered by an observed live worker window whose title showed 'Select Administrator: Hermes Remote Worker ...' while output appeared frozen beyond the nominal 300s idle watchdog. In classic Windows console, Select/QuickEdit mode can pause console application progress. The active E3 gate had already landed commit 91a2adc2 while the visible wrapper remained open, consistent with a finalization/console interaction stall. This task should prevent recurrence without sacrificing visible worker output. Owner clarification 2026-09-24: on a recoverable worker failure, retry the SAME task twice before blocking/advancing. This is distinct from the Stage-2 missing-key anti-loop rule: deterministic credential blockers must not be retried while the credential state is unchanged.
